name: Three Nought Four
description: 304 is a trick-taking partnership game for four. 32-card deck. Card values: J=30, 9=20, A=11, 10=10, K=3, Q=2, 8=7=0. Total 304 points. Bid from 160 in tens; highest bidder sets trump face-down then remaining cards dealt. Follow suit; bidding team must make bid in points. Popular in Sri Lanka and India.

history.origins: Sri Lanka and coastal India (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra). Named after 304 total points.
timeline: 20th century: Popular in Sri Lanka and coastal India; cited as ancestor of Twenty-eight.

setup.players: Four players in two fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite (e.g. North-South vs East-West). Deal and play are counter-clockwise.
setup.deck: A standard 32-card pack: 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in all four suits (spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts). Total point value in the pack is 304.
setup.dealing: Four cards at a time counter-clockwise; after bid, rest dealt; trump face-down.

rules.objective: Each team aims to bid a number (in multiples of 10, from 160 upward) and then win at least that many card points in tricks. The bidding team wins the hand if they make their bid; otherwise the opponents win.
rules.gameplay: Bid from 160. Trump maker places trump face-down. Follow suit. J=30, 9=20, A=11, 10=10, K=3, Q=2, 8=7=0.

strategy.intermediate: Count point cards (J=30, 9=20, A=11, 10=10); bid with strong trump and point cards.
strategy.advanced: Partnership: signal through leads; defend by taking point cards when opponents bid.
tips: 304 points total in deck; bid from 160.
Trump face-down; plan to make bid in trick points.

scoring.description: Bidding team wins if trick points meet or exceed bid.
scoring.winCondition: Bid and make at least the bid in points.
